selection.summary: Reviewed src/user/email.js base logic for the reported confirmation inconsistency. Key findings: (1) UserEmail.isValidationPending (h5/h12 area) returns true if confirm:byUid:<uid> exists, and with an email arg compares against the confirm object — a mismatched/stale email can cause inconsistent pending status. (2) sendValidationEmail (h7/h8) blocks resends by checking isValidationPending(uid, email); since the confirm:byUid key expires after emailConfirmInterval (pexpireAt at Date.now() + emailInterval*60*1000, h14/h13), resend is blocked exactly for the configured interval and allowed again once expired — consistent with expected behavior, provided emailInterval is configured correctly (unclear/long expiry in the report may be a config issue). (3) The confirm:<code> object has a fixed 24-hour TTL (h14: expireAt +60*60*24) independent of emailConfirmInterval, so old confirmations can outlive the byUid key — potential source of 'old confirmations remain active' if code TTL is intended to match the confirm interval. (4) expireValidation (h5) deletes both confirm:byUid:<uid> and confirm:<code>, so after expiring, resending is immediately allowed; but if only one key is cleared (e.g., code object expires first while byUid remains, or vice versa), stale state can block or misreport pending status. (5) On send, expireValidation is called before setting new keys (h7), which is correct ordering. Base test coverage (h3, h10) exercises pending validation, confirmation via API, and 403/404 paths, but does not cover resend-after-expiry timing or TTL boundary behavior. No repair has been applied; these are delivered base observations only. Recommend verifying config emailConfirmInterval, aligning confirm:<code> TTL with the configured interval, and hardening isValidationPending to verify both keys agree.
